newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices recover on warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices recover on warmer weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices rebounded Wednesday as warmer weather returned to Texas and cooling demand remained strong throughout most of the Southwest, market sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average gained four cents to $2.20-2.23 per mmBtu, while Transco (Station 65) was also quoted mostly in the low-$2.20s.
The work on Transco's Texas line will also continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
Helping to alleviate some of the supply tightness will be the expected restart on Thursday of Entergy Corp's 936 megawatt River Bend nuclear unit in Louisiana.
In south Texas, prices rose one cent to about $2.10.
In the East, New York city-gate prices were steady to higher in the mid-$2.40s.
Temperatures throughout the Northeast are expected to remain slightly below normal through the week, Weather Services Corp said.
Appalachian prices also climbed about four cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are still at least five degrees below normal, prices gained about five cents to $2.00-2.05.
Chicago city-gate was quoted in the low-$2.30s.
In west Texas, Permian prices jumped seven cents to an average of $2 as temperatures in the Southwest continued to defy seasonal norms.

Also as a result of the heat, Waha prices edged up six cents to $2.03-2.06. At the southern California border, prices eased by about two cents to $2.15 as temperatures on the West Coast hovered only slightly above normal.
